Aerial snow: historical 15–60 cm aggregates lack a calibrated whole-aggregate fracture law. The conservative checkpoint repairs particle bookkeeping, but heavy lunar controls fail the finite mass-domain check. Independent characteristics isolate first-order deposition spreading; positive limited transport reduces excess relative mass variance by 93.1% at 144 pivots against the once-projected reference. Completed limited-growth lunar controls still lose 60.37% and 58.08% of supplied mass at 96 and 144 pivots. A quadratic geometry continuation above a diagnostic 1 cm join reduces loss to 14.22% on the same 96 mass pivots and still fails. An exact-event capture reference now isolates collision-grid spreading: at 96 pivots its variance is about 95,125 times the reference despite a mean difference of only 0.00279%. A bounded beta moment candidate agrees with late prescribed-bath endpoints but misses an analytic cell-crossing number CDF by 18.4 percentage points despite accurate mean and variance. An entropy alternative reduces the analytic crossing CDF error to 0.185 percentage points but its original explicit time-stepping refinements hit runtime limits. Finite-time Poisson capture and size-dependent birth updates now complete six analytic and six physical-bath controls, satisfying declared distribution, moment, accounting and truncation criteria. Maximum analytic CDF error is 0.258 percentage points; the physical controls remain compatible with the 8192-history reference under its per-time sampling band. The initial doubled-quadrature control hit a 300-second wall limit; a separately bound continuation repeats that setting with a larger execution allowance while retaining the other five completed controls unchanged. This establishes a maintained-bath component; donor-depleting closed aggregation and the coupled lunar column remain untested with it, and no full-column replacement is adopted. Ordinary six-hour bulk statistics improve with refinement; twelve-hour finite-volume convergence fails and the coupled tail remains unresolved. A separate published Earth deposition/settling comparison gives integrated raw-profile differences of 0.55–1.77%, with 7.62% number-density error in the source region and 31.2% excess in its top bin after height refinement. A separate compact-sphere capacitance sensitivity reduces source-belt number-density error to 3.14% and top-bin error to 15.0%, with full sensitivity convergence and physical adoption unestablished. Its exact archived executable remains unidentified; a pinned public-source author aggregation rerun now supplies a declared-setting comparison with material 12.5–16.5% total-profile differences and 70.1% aggregate number-density difference, while independent coupled aggregation, breakup population comparisons and empirical validation remain unperformed. The Böhm adapter reproduces 122 author-code cases and five archived Earth surface cases under stated air assumptions; applicability to giant porous aggregates is unestablished. Selected fixed-drift paths through a 35-hour older A28_dim5 storm have median cumulative moist exposures of 26–30.5 minutes; conditional release, censoring, field cadence and coarse spatial resolution preclude flake-lifetime or climate-frequency claims. Distribution, time, vertical and domain convergence, evolving geometry, contact-network strength, largest-remnant breakup, resolved moist growth histories and calibrated lunar size/optical distributions remain unresolved. See atmosphere/snow/collision_jump_results.md, collision_repair.md, collision_and_exposure.md, growth_repair.md and welss_column.md.

Snow optics: geometric-area extinction and height-resolved incident lunar light are calculated with explicit phase and cloud-water sensitivities. The 294.9 K optical column differs from the 301 K snow column. Direction-dependent aggregate area, calibrated phase matrices, the Earthlight spectrum and joint transport through a finite evolving snow/liquid cloud remain unresolved.

Full prescribed lunar snow column: the donor-depleting event solver completes 512 independent closed-box controls and 28 full Earth/lunar columns; lunar mass medians 12.3, 18.5 and 23.5 cm and mean 99th percentiles 19.8, 36.3 and 74.1 cm fail volume convergence. A separate 48-column diagnosis preserves all original outputs and accounts for changing vapour uptake: gathering deposition is 2.199, 2.373 and 2.498 mm/h under a 3 mm/h cap, while lowest-layer empty fractions are 64.3%, 40.7% and 7.5%. The nonlinear averaging effect peaks higher up where demand crosses the cap; its frozen-history allocation gap falls from 0.467 to 0.132 mm/h. Removing all collisions passes the tested volume screen. Growth-disabled, chipping-disabled and both-disabled columns retain failed upper-tail checks; the sticking-only 99th-percentile change is 22.5% with appreciable four-realization uncertainty. The half-step water diagnosis changes little while its size distribution still fails the existing screen. Water conservation, passive-observer identity and these controls do not establish a converged lunar population or an empirical aggregate limit. Further finite-population and time controls, a tested numerical replacement, aggregate geometry and fracture, and climate-supported water histories remain open; a shared-demand experiment is proposed, not adopted. See atmosphere/snow/column_diagnosis_results.md and event_column_results.md. No new storm optical forecast is adopted.

Snow solver reuse: ten full-duration SCALE executions and four additional custom controls now compare the original 16.28 km, 132.59 h lunar forcing. Native SCALE medians remain 1.58–1.59 mm and p99 3.10–3.14 mm under particle/time/height refinements; the original stronger sticking law gives 3.56/7.47 mm with zero collision omissions at 15 s. Custom ballistic/no-chipping medians remain 14–18 cm and change with statistical volume. Similar prescribed water fluxes coexist with very different particle numbers, masses and geometry. The full comparison establishes model dependence, not a unique diagnosis of the older solver's volume limit. A finite-vapor control with maintained temperature remains millimetric; an uncooled thermal control warms toward freezing and delivers rain. Published Earth population reproduction, complete energy accounting, justified lunar cooling/moisture histories and contact fracture remain open; no storm optical forecast is adopted. See atmosphere/snow/scale_lunar_results.md and results/scale_lunar_comparison.json.

Snow size attribution: matched SCALE controls produce larger lunar snow than the shallow Earth-gravity counterpart (about 1.59 versus 0.744–0.746 mm mass median). Lower gravity and deeper cloud each enhance aggregation. The prescribed 3 mm/h source and 10232 crystals/m2/s limit potential deposited mass to 0.081 mg per entering crystal; geometry and aggregation determine how it becomes arriving flakes. The small absolute sizes therefore occur in a shared prescribed regime, not through an identified lunar-only suppression. A tenfold seed reduction raises the lunar median to 3.32 mm; tenfold water raises it to 4.53 mm after refinement. Final Earth bulk changes are below 0.8%, but the exact distribution still fails timestep refinement (7.19 percentage points versus a 5-point criterion). Gravity-independent aggregate compaction, observed Earth population reproduction and weather-supported sources remain unresolved. See atmosphere/snow/scale_size_results.md for completed controls and numerical limits; no empirical lunar size bound or storm optics are adopted.

SCALE growth and geometry: five new full-column controls show experimental offset contacts raising lunar mass median/D99 from 1.59/3.11 to 2.74/7.82 mm. The lunar timestep screen passes; the Earth exact mass-distribution screen fails at 6.42 percentage points despite bulk changes below 0.87%. Five isolated growth executions compare the -14.4 C Takahashi 1991 Earth fit: observed fitted width at 30 min is 4.17 mm, while native SCALE gives 27.66 mm from the fitted thin initial crystal and 0.96 mm from a sphere with the same initial mass and span. The final Earth timestep refinement changes width by 0.81%, much less than the discrepancy. The integrated simulated thickness/width growth ratio is 0.112 versus 0.509 from the observed fits; coupled habit, density, capacitance and ventilation require diagnosis across more temperatures before production adoption. This is a specific empirical growth failure and an experimental geometry sensitivity, not a lunar size ceiling, a validated replacement closure or an observed aggregate population. Fifty physics inputs reproduce byte-for-byte; zero-change geometry matches all arrivals and 81 native history arrays. See atmosphere/snow/scale_limitations.md.

SCALE growth across habits: ten native executions at five Earth laboratory temperatures give endpoint mass/fit ratios 1.41–19.10, with short columns and wide plates. Four instrumented controls isolate directional ventilation: removing its axis preference reduces the -14.4 C, 30-minute width from 27.66 to 15.81 mm versus the fitted 4.17 mm, and mass from 1.392 to 0.798 mg versus 0.0729 mg. Numerical refinement is much smaller; native and instrumented zero-change paths reproduce ledger bytes and all 473 particle/history arrays at both steps. Five additional three-minute fitted mass/axes combinations exceed native bulk density when represented as spheroids and are explicitly rejected. A recovered 169-row laboratory dataset retains missing axes and unresolved data flags. Newer McSnow growth/2026 geometry and exoplanet CARMA approaches were reviewed, not newly validated or adopted; low-pressure source access and directly matched sustained lunar-gravity growth data remain incomplete. See atmosphere/snow/growth_benchmarks.md and growth_options.md; no new physical lunar-size or optical forecast is adopted.

Native McSnow growth: 80 matched Earth process cases plus five selected refinements compare 2024/2026 source, original/revised growth packages, fitted three-minute states and age-zero 2 micrometre-radius spheres. Seventy-five executions complete; ten dendritic fitted starts fail with uncontrolled growth and trapped floating-point errors. The revised spherical dendrite is fairly close to the fit at ten minutes but reaches 195.39 mm and 1777 times fitted mass at thirty minutes, versus fitted width 4.17 mm. Final seed refinement changes that width by 0.389%; failed trajectories remain late-time sensitive and have no accepted endpoint. Selected compact-crystal improvements do not resolve mass and both axes across habits. Sphere histories agree between source versions to roundoff; porous-restart differences involve two newer deposition-density rules. Coupled directional and shape-dependent mean ventilation are identified control targets, not a calibrated causal repair. Exact published-figure reproduction, low-pressure/humidity transfer, aggregation fracture and lunar storm optics remain unresolved. See atmosphere/snow/mcsnow_growth.md.

Earth growth repair assessment: 240 ventilation controls causally identify the extra thin-plate mean term as the main late-runaway contribution. Revised spherical-start width at 30 min falls from 195.39 to 5.88 mm when removed, and 4.68 mm with unit directional ratio, versus 4.17 mm fitted; fitted restarts and other habits retain errors. Another 288 humidity/seed-history executions expose strong dependence on unreported initial shape, growth package and branching history; selecting a favorable seed is not validation. Conditional transport with observed axes/speed gives much closer mass, but native-versus-mixture diffusivity differs by 15%, source-Schmidt sensitivity matters, and agreement with the published Westbrook-Heymsfield2011 comparison remains to be reconciled. Four previously rejected initial states reflect hexagonal/spheroidal volume mapping. A published facet-attachment component and dense stagnant-growth prototype are implemented and tested as development controls, not adopted as a complete replacement. Early-state geometry, branching/hollowing density, consistent ventilated surface kinetics, lower-pressure validation and aggregate fracture remain open. The reference lunar winter pressure of 414-659 hPa overlaps terrestrial laboratory physics. See atmosphere/snow/earth_growth_assessment.md; no physical lunar size or optical forecast is adopted.

Hollow-crystal repair: 2026 published geometry routines reproduce 17000 archived numbers within 2.48e-6 relative error; a guarded local interface rejects eight converted hexagonal states beyond the source fit interval. Two substrate series provide 94 axis/rim measurements; a -50 C humidity step from 48% to 20% ice supersaturation widens the median rim by 3.58 times (2.65-4.57 under reported measurement-error bounds). Post-step derivative ratios remain unresolved under conservative errors. Sixty-nine warm size comparisons reuse the 1991 experiment, and eleven separate early points are duplicates. Full 2026 growth equations were not obtained (publisher 403, first-page author preview); the archive is a geometry component, not a complete growth solver. Joint mass/axes/rim evolution, lower-pressure validation and lunar aggregates remain open. See atmosphere/snow/earth_growth_assessment.md and results/hollow_growth_assessment.json.

Explicit face-transport repair: 534 of 738 requested measured-shape comparisons calculate at two tolerances, with 180 unsupported-ventilation and 24 out-of-fit-geometry requests rejected. Of 516 solid-face hypotheses, 387 fail sampled necessary uniform-growth conditions. Warm-column common-corner growth produces basal-centre undersaturation; 18 prescribed narrow-rim sensitivities do not jointly repair mass and both axes. The inherited 2021 routine sets equal facet characteristics below -30 C; in the cylindrical common-corner model this forces equal axis speeds, excluded in two cold-chamber windows under reported measurement-error bounds. The third window remains unresolved, and all 94 measured rims exceed the declared narrow-ring regime. Full spatial hollow/branched geometry, independent facet kinetics and source locations remain necessary; complete 2026 equations remain unretrieved. See atmosphere/snow/earth_growth_assessment.md and results/uniform_face_assessment.json.

Surface transfer: 158 frozen-profile calculations conserve gas uptake and donor/recipient mass. At the eight-minute warm state, assumed 5 micrometre migration raises mean tip growth from 0.277 to 0.836 of the fitted rate at nearly fixed uptake, while 14 nm reaches 0.280. Prism migration and edge transmission are unmeasured; later separate sheaths and specimen-to-specimen variation are not represented by an axisymmetric ring. Direct prism-step microscopy does not provide a universal normal-growth law, and the 2026 nitrogen-pressure main paper remains unretrieved despite its public abstract and supplement. Moving profiles, joint Earth validation and lunar transfer remain open. See atmosphere/snow/earth_growth_assessment.md.
